title: harnessed stack
description: A harness-free composition of recipes (catalog/stacks/<name>/stack.yaml). The harness is chosen at run time as a required CLI argument. Nothing is resolved at runtime; recipes are assembled ahead of time. See docs/harnessed-design.md §5/§12.

name.description: Stack identity. Convention: <recipe>[_<recipe>…] (hyphens allowed within a name). Must not equal a harness name.

extends.description: Inherit from another stack (by name; resolved in this catalog root first, then the catalog search path — so an overlay stack may extend one shipped in the repo). recipes/services/harnesses/ssh_keys UNION with the parent's (parent's first, then this stack's, de-duped); every other field this stack declares overrides the parent's, and any it omits is inherited. Chains are allowed; cycles are an error.

permissions.description: Permission mode written into the profile as Claude's permissions.defaultMode. Claude's own mode names pass through verbatim (acceptEdits, auto, bypassPermissions, default, dontAsk, plan); 'prompt' and 'yolo' are aliases for 'default' and 'bypassPermissions'. Unset means 'acceptEdits' — safe in an isolated instance. Note 'auto' is Claude's real auto mode and is NOT the same as 'acceptEdits'.

instructions.description: Stack-level identity text emitted into the profile's .claude/CLAUDE.md at assemble time — 'what is this assembled agent'. Distinct from recipe-level rules (per-recipe RULE.md files). Claude-only.

recipes.description: Recipe names composed onto the harness, in declaration order. Each must resolve in the catalog (user overlay first, then repo).

services.description: Shared services attached by reference. Started host-published, idempotently, outliving the instance.

harnesses.description: Harnesses this stack is built for. Build-time only — the harness is still a run-time CLI argument, so the stack stays harness-independent. `harnessed build <stack>` (no harness) fans out to every name listed here, and a bare `harnessed build` includes these (stack, harness) pairs in its reconciliation sweep. Omit to require an explicit harness argument.

forward_git_credentials.description: Opt-in (default false): forward the SECRET-BEARING slice of the host's git push surface — the gh oauth token (~/.config/gh/hosts.yml), opt-in private SSH keys, ssh config/known_hosts/pubkeys, and non-secret gnupg files. The SSH signing/auth agent socket (1Password/gpg-agent) plus the ro git identity config are forwarded AUTOMATICALLY whenever the host agent is live, independent of this flag — set this only to also mount the gh token / private keys.

ssh_keys.description: Private-key basenames under ~/.ssh to mount read-only into the container, for hosts without an SSH agent. Each entry is a single path component (no '/' or '..'). Honored ONLY from the user overlay catalog, never a shared-catalog stack. Requires forward_git_credentials.

forward_aws_sso.description: Opt-in (default false): forward host AWS credentials via the aws-sso ECS server (aws-sso-cli, default slot). When true and the host has run `harnessed aws-sso serve`, the launcher injects AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_FULL_URI + AWS_CONTAINER_AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN as env so the in-container AWS SDK pulls short-lived STS creds over HTTP — no aws-sso binary, ~/.aws-sso store, or SSO token enters the container. SECRET-BEARING (STS creds are not touch-gated), hence opt-in. No-op when the host token file is absent. See docs/guides/aws-sso.md.

isolated_auth.description: Opt-in (default false): give this stack its OWN Claude identity instead of the host's, so it can run as a DIFFERENT account (a client's). The host CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is withheld (env forward AND --env-file) and no host credential file is seeded; the stack gets a per-instance credentials file it logs into itself, persisted across recreates and cleared by `--fresh`. Does not breach 'credentials referenced, never replicated' — nothing is copied, so there is no second copy to diverge. Simpler alternative when the client hands you a token outright: put CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN in <project>/.env.schema, which takes precedence. claude only.

hub_transport.description: How the harness reaches the hatago hub. 'http' (default) runs hatago as a long-lived in-container server that every client in the container shares. 'stdio' makes the harness spawn its own hub, which costs that sharing (two clients mean two hubs, and two copies of every stdio child) and buys two things http cannot give an OAuth-bearing child server: Claude Code no longer treats the hub as a REMOTE server, so authenticating it stops running Dynamic Client Registration against a hub that has no such endpoint (observed: 'SDK auth failed: Dynamic Client Registration rejected (HTTP 404)'); and a child's stderr — where mcp-remote prints its 'Please authorize this client by visiting:' URL — reaches the harness instead of /tmp/hatago.log, where nobody sees it. Honoured only by harnesses whose hub entry harnessed emits (claude); codex and omp bake the hub address into their image, so declaring stdio for them is a build-time error.

state.description: State and lifecycle options. Default persistent; `--fresh` overrides at runtime.

persist.description: Keep state across runs (default true). `--fresh` at runtime forces a throwaway volume.

session_state.description: Where Claude session state (projects/ + history.jsonl) lives. 'host' (default) persists to a harnessed-owned host dir, inspectable; 'volume' uses a throwaway per-instance volume.
